findings.evidence: "Similarly, the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral transition such as "In addition," or state the cadence difference directly, e.g. "On a different schedule, the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month."
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies the equipment catalog update follows the same pattern as the reimbursement log update, but the reimbursement log updates once a year at the start of the fiscal year while the equipment catalog updates monthly. The connector misstates the relationship between the two facts.

findings.evidence: "the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month" (Program Overview); "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year" (Special Cases); "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year" (Questions and Updates)
findings.fix: Identify a single owner and a single update cadence for the equipment catalog, and correct or remove the other two mentions.
findings.location: "Program Overview," "Special Cases," and "Questions and Updates" sections
findings.violation: The document names three different owners (IT asset group, finance liaison, benefits team) and two different cadences (monthly, annually) for what appears to be the same equipment catalog, without reconciling the conflict.

findings.evidence: "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year." (Eligibility); "the policy applies to one device per category per employee." (Restrictions and Exceptions)
findings.fix: State explicitly whether the per-benefit-year limit is one claim in total or one device per category, and remove whichever statement is incorrect.
findings.location: "Eligibility" section, first paragraph, and "Restrictions and Exceptions" section, second paragraph
findings.violation: The eligibility section limits an employee to one claim per benefit year, while the restrictions section implies an employee may claim one device per category, which would allow more than one claim per year if more than one category applies. The two limits are never reconciled.

findings.evidence: "an incomplete request pauses the timeline until the missing item arrives"
findings.fix: Name the specific item or items that can be missing, for example a receipt or a completed form field, or cross-reference the "Required Documentation" section.
findings.violation: "the missing item" has no antecedent anywhere in the document. Nothing earlier lists what could be missing from a request.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: State where this review falls in the approval sequence and whether it adds time beyond the two-business-day timeline.
findings.violation: This introduces a second, dollar-triggered review step that is never connected to the two-business-day manager review described in "Approval Timeline," leaving the total approval time for requests over 200 dollars undefined.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, for example "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence switches to second person ("You," "we"), while the rest of the document refers to "employees," "the employee," and "the manager" in third person.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Either define "stipend item" explicitly, including how it differs from "stipend," or rename the section to describe what it actually contains, and rewrite it in third person to match the rest of the document.
findings.violation: A section titled "Terminology Notes" is expected to define terms, but this section only repeats the phrase "stipend item" three times without ever defining it or distinguishing it from "stipend." It also uses second person, unlike the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Merge this content into "How to Apply," reconciling the two descriptions of the process, and remove the separate section.
findings.violation: This section describes the start of the request process, but it duplicates and conflicts with "How to Apply," which already describes starting a request through the benefits portal and never mentions confirming eligibility or uploading a receipt as first steps. Its placement, after "Terminology Notes" and before "Special Cases," is also disconnected from the earlier process sections.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a transition that does not assert a false parallel, such as "Separately," or move this sentence to the "Eligibility" section where the claim limit is discussed.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies this statement follows the same logic as the preceding sentence about equipment condition and photo checks, but a device-per-category limit is an unrelated claim-count rule, not a similar restriction.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: Specify which requests require more than a photo receipt and what additional documentation applies, or remove "most" if a photo is always sufficient.
findings.violation: "most requests" implies some requests need more than a photo of the receipt, but the document never states which requests those are or what additional documentation they require.
